intent: Fix #34384: keep users logged in across SECRET_KEY rotation when the old key is in SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS. Adds AbstractBaseUser.get_session_auth_fallback_hash(); get_user() accepts a session hash that matches a fallback key, cycles the session key, and rewrites the stored hash with the current key. 4.1.8 bugfix backport; must not weaken invalidation on password change or break custom user models.

findings.title: get_user() raises AttributeError for duck-typed users with a stale session hash
findings.suggested_fix: Treat the fallback method as optional, matching the existing hasattr() duck-typing: `get_fallback = getattr(user, "get_session_auth_fallback_hash", None)`, then only run `any(constant_time_compare(session_hash, h) for h in get_fallback())` when it is callable; otherwise fall through to `request.session.flush(); user = None` as before. Add a TestGetUser case with a backend returning a plain object that defines get_session_auth_hash() but not get_session_auth_fallback_hash(), a stale HASH_SESSION_KEY, asserting AnonymousUser is returned and the session is flushed, with and without SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS set.
findings.why_it_matters: get_user() decides whether to verify the session with hasattr(user, "get_session_auth_hash"), and the docs explicitly support user models that do not inherit AbstractBaseUser but implement their own get_session_auth_hash(). The new mismatch branch unconditionally calls user.get_session_auth_fallback_hash(), which exists only on AbstractBaseUser and is new in the 4.1.8 patch release. For such a duck-typed user model, any stored hash that does not match (the documented logout-on-password-change path, or a SECRET_KEY rotation) now raises AttributeError instead of flushing the session and returning AnonymousUser. The session is never flushed, so every later request carrying that cookie (including via AuthenticationMiddleware's lazy request.user / request.auser()) returns a 500 until the cookie is cleared. This narrows a documented contract in a bugfix release with no release note. No in-tree class hits it; the impact falls on third-party user classes.

django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:141 -- def get_session_auth_fallback_hash(self): (defined only on AbstractBaseUser, new in this diff)

docs/topics/auth/default.txt:920-923 -- 'If your AUTH_USER_MODEL inherits from AbstractBaseUser or implements its own get_session_auth_hash() method, authenticated sessions will include the hash returned by this function.'
docs/topics/auth/customizing.txt:727 -- '.. versionadded:: 4.1.8' (new method added in a patch release; no note that custom non-AbstractBaseUser models must now implement it)

Reproduced in scratch against the reviewed tree (reviewers and validator): backend returning a plain class defining only get_session_auth_hash(), session HASH_SESSION_KEY='stale' -> get_user() raises AttributeError: 'U' object has no attribute 'get_session_auth_fallback_hash' instead of flushing and returning AnonymousUser
Cascade: stale hash -> AttributeError before request.session.flush() -> session persists -> every later request that touches request.user raises again
findings.validation_reason: django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:200 gates only on hasattr(user, 'get_session_auth_hash') while the diff-added line 215 unconditionally calls user.get_session_auth_fallback_hash() (defined only on AbstractBaseUser), docs/topics/auth/default.txt:920-923 documents duck-typed models implementing only get_session_auth_hash(), and my scratch-validator/repro.py at HEAD 2396933ca9 (plain U with only get_session_auth_hash, stale HASH_SESSION_KEY, signed_cookies session) raised AttributeError instead of flushing and returning AnonymousUser; no in-tree caller produces such a user, so real-world incidence among third-party models was not measured.

findings.title: Fallback-configured reject path untested; accept-all mutation survives
findings.suggested_fix: In TestGetUser, add a test that logs in, changes the user's password (or stores a hash computed with an unrelated key), then calls get_user() under override_settings(SECRET_KEY='newsecret', SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS=[old_key]) and asserts that the result is AnonymousUser and request.session.session_key is None. Optionally add a table-driven case where the fallback list contains several non-matching keys.
findings.first_evidence: django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:213-216 -- if session_hash and any(constant_time_compare(session_hash, fallback_auth_hash) for fallback_auth_hash in user.get_session_auth_fallback_hash()):
findings.why_it_matters: The stated intent includes 'must not weaken session invalidation on password change'. The only new test covers the case where the fallback matches. The only existing invalidation test (test_middleware.test_changed_password_invalidates_session) runs with SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS=[], so any([]) is False and the test cannot tell whether the fallback comparison works. In a scratch copy I replaced the any(constant_time_compare(...)) check with `session_hash and settings.SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS`, which accepts any stale hash whenever fallbacks are configured. All of auth_tests still passed (Ran 607 tests, OK). A future refactor that keeps sessions alive after a password change during key rotation would therefore ship with green tests.

triage_groups.title: get_user() fallback branch: guard the new call and test both mismatch outcomes
triage_groups.context: Both findings sit in the new mismatch branch of get_user() (django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:213-221) and both fixes add TestGetUser cases next to test_get_user_fallback_secret.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Handle #1 first: make get_session_auth_fallback_hash optional via getattr and add the duck-typed stale-hash test; then add #2's negative test (fallbacks configured, hash matches no key -> flushed, AnonymousUser).
triage_groups.why: #1 is a runtime regression for custom user models; #2 locks in that the fallback path never weakens invalidation on password change.

residual_risks.text: AbstractBaseUser subclasses that override get_session_auth_hash() (extra fields, different salt) do not get matching fallback hashes: get_session_auth_fallback_hash() always calls the base _get_session_auth_hash(), so those projects still lose every session on SECRET_KEY rotation and the docs do not tell overriders to override both. Fails safe; the fix silently does not apply to them.
evidence: django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:143 -- yield self._get_session_auth_hash(secret=fallback_secret)
django/contrib/auth/base_user.py:139 -- return self._get_session_auth_hash()

residual_risks.text: On the first request after rotation, get_user() calls request.session.cycle_key(), which creates a new key and deletes the old session row on db/cache backends; parallel in-flight requests still carrying the old cookie can load an empty session (AnonymousUser, and SessionMiddleware may send delete_cookie that races the new cookie) or leave an orphaned row. Not a regression from 4.1 (those sessions were previously invalidated outright); updating HASH_SESSION_KEY without cycle_key() would avoid it.
evidence: django/contrib/auth/__init__.py:217 -- request.session.cycle_key()
django/contrib/sessions/backends/base.py:298-307 -- cycle_key(): self.create(); ... if key: self.delete(key)
django/contrib/sessions/middleware.py:36 -- if settings.SESSION_COOKIE_NAME in request.COOKIES and empty: response.delete_cookie(...)

testing_gaps.text: No test that a session with no HASH_SESSION_KEY is still flushed (AnonymousUser returned) when SECRET_KEY_FALLBACKS is non-empty; this guards the `session_hash and` short-circuit in the fallback branch.
